hero.title: Activities
hero.subtitle: There is always something to do. And always space to do nothing at all.

intro:
Life on Sømliøya happens mostly outside.

The island and the surrounding fjord offer space for simple things: exploring the landscape, spending time by the water, or gathering around a fire. There is always something to do — and, of course, always space to do nothing at all.

items.imageAlt: View across the fjord with a small boat
items.title: Kayaking
items.description: The sheltered waters around the island are ideal for kayaking. Follow the coastline, explore small bays or paddle out between the scattered islands. On calm mornings the water can be almost mirror-like.

items.imageAlt: Fishing rods against the fjord with mountain backdrop
items.title: Fishing
items.description: FFishing is part of everyday life here. Cast a line from the shore or head out by boat and, depending on the season, you may catch cod, pollock, mackerel or even a helibot!

items.imageAlt: Person fishing from rocks in Norwegian sweater
items.title: Swimming
items.description: The sea rarely gets warm, even in summer. A swim from the rocks is refreshing and warming up afterwards by the sun or the fire makes it worth it every time.

items.imageAlt: Two hikers at mountain summit at sunset
items.title: Walking & Hiking
items.description: From the island you can wander along the shoreline, through quiet forest and over smooth coastal rocks. There are no crowds or marked tourist routes, just nature at its own pace and endless mountains.

items.imageAlt: Silhouette of hiker against dramatic orange sunset
items.title: Heilhornet
items.description: Rising directly from the coast, Heilhornet is one of the region's most recognisable mountains. The hike takes around six hours, but the reward is a sweeping view across the Helgeland coastline, the fjords and the Norwegian Sea.

items.imageAlt: Hikers on rocky mountain summit ridge
items.title: Wildlife Watching
items.description: Sea eagles are often seen above the fjord, and roe deer and moose move through nearby forests.

regionSection.heading: Exploring the Region

places.name: Island of Leka
places.description:
Leka is a small island off the coast, known for its distinctive red and orange rock formations — some of the oldest geological formations in the country. The landscape is surprisingly varied, with rugged mountains, open coastline, quiet beaches, and wide views over the sea.

It is also home to what is often considered one of the most beautiful hikes in Norway, with trails that take you through this unique geology and out to panoramic coastal views.

![Leka's red rock formations and coastline](/images/IMG_6617.jpeg)

places.name: Coastal Villages
places.description: The mainland coast nearby is dotted with small fishing villages and quiet harbours. A short trip by boat brings you to shops, cafés and the everyday rhythm of Norwegian coastal life — close enough to reach with ease, far enough that the island remains its own quiet world.

regionSection.imageAlt: Two people at summit cairn overlooking fjords at sunset

fireSection.heading: Around the Fire
fireSection.text:
As the light softens, the day usually finds its way back to the fire. It is where meals are cooked and shared, where stories are told, and where the evening slows to the sound of the water.

A fire by the shore is the simplest thing the island offers — and often the part of a stay that people remember most.
